title: sub_resource ID is not stable after first save
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.6.3

### System information

Windows 10 - Godot v4.6.3.stable - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970

### Issue description

sub_resource IDs stored in a saved (.tres) resource are not stable after first save.
The second save of the resource modifies the sub_resource IDs.
Successive saves do not modify the sub_resource IDs anymore.

I have tried adding `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().scan()` and other editor specific refreshes/forced reloads but they don't seem to work.

### Steps to reproduce

Make a few resource classes:
`fruit_resource.gd`:
```gdscript
class_name Fruit
extends Resource

@export var id := &""

```

`basket_resource.gd`:
```gdscript
class_name Basket
extends Resource

@export var fruits: Array[Fruit] = []

```

Also create an editor script:
`run.gd`:
```gdscript
@tool
extends EditorScript

const BASKET_PATH := "res://resources/basket.tres"

func _run():
	print("Creating or loading basket with path '%s'" % [BASKET_PATH])
	var basket := load_or_create_resource(BASKET_PATH, Basket) as Basket

	var starfruit := Fruit.new()
	starfruit.id = &"starfruit"

	basket.fruits.clear()
	basket.fruits.append(starfruit)

	ResourceSaver.save(basket)

	var content := FileAccess.get_file_as_string(BASKET_PATH)
	print(content)

func load_or_create_resource(path: String, script_class: GDScript) -> Resource:
	if ResourceLoader.exists(path):
		return load(path)

	print(script_class)
	var resource: Resource = script_class.new()
	resource.take_over_path(path)
	return resource
```

The first time you run this script, the following result is printed to the console:
```
Creating or loading basket with path 'res://resources/basket.tres'
(res://basket_resource.gd):<GDScript#-9223370357337944063>
[gd_resource type="Resource" script_class="Basket" format=3 uid="uid://b3fx32glo6lmo"]

[ext_resource type="Script" uid="uid://brdc4lukbmvvj" path="res://fruit_resource.gd" id="1_6sqqn"]
[ext_resource type="Script" uid="uid://deiory2etv2in" path="res://basket_resource.gd" id="2_s17x4"]

[sub_resource type="Resource" id="Resource_elwjf"]
script = ExtResource("1_6sqqn")
id = &"starfruit"

[resource]
script = ExtResource("2_s17x4")
fruits = Array[ExtResource("1_6sqqn")]([SubResource("Resource_elwjf")])
```
Second time (and all consecutive times after that):
```
Creating or loading basket with path 'res://resources/basket.tres'
[gd_resource type="Resource" script_class="Basket" format=3 uid="uid://b3fx32glo6lmo"]

[ext_resource type="Script" uid="uid://brdc4lukbmvvj" path="res://fruit_resource.gd" id="1_6sqqn"]
[ext_resource type="Script" uid="uid://deiory2etv2in" path="res://basket_resource.gd" id="2_s17x4"]

[sub_resource type="Resource" id="Resource_6sqqn"]
script = ExtResource("1_6sqqn")
id = &"starfruit"

[resource]
script = ExtResource("2_s17x4")
fruits = Array[ExtResource("1_6sqqn")]([SubResource("Resource_6sqqn")])
```

Thus the sub_resource ID of the fruit has been changed from `Resource_elwjf` to `Resource_6sqqn`.

Am I missing any way to force Godot to immediately use the normalized sub_resource IDs?
I tried using `scan()` etc. but to no avail.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[saving-resources.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28781952/saving-resources.zip)
